outcome: umbilical cord arterial blood gas measures (pH, PCO2, PO2, HCO3, base deficit)
neonatal outcomes (birthweight, 1-minute Apgar scores, 5-minute Apgar scores, resuscitation, NICU admissions)
cohort: The study included term singleton pregnancies (gestational age >= 37 weeks) that underwent elective cesarean sections from four hospitals in Iran, excluding those with various maternal pre-existing conditions or substance use.
finding: Pregnancies with GDM showed significantly lower umbilical cord arterial pH and greater base deficit, indicating higher umbilical cord blood acidity and impaired placental function, despite no differences in mean birthweight or Apgar scores.
mod_finding: The study cohort exclusively consisted of pregnancies that underwent elective cesarean sections, so mode of birth was a fixed characteristic rather than a varying finding.
birth_weight: mean birthweight was measured, but no significant difference was found between GDM and non-GDM groups.
